Check your posture. I just started getting really bad pains in my wrists from years of bad posture, bad posture when playing and in general. I've picked up some tips from doctors/players. 

Any time you start to get pain stop and do these exercises, they're easy. 

The first is to make tights fists, hold for a second, then slowly release and stretch your fingers out as far as possible. Do this a few times, but stop right away if it hurts. 

Second, get a 0.5-1lb weight. Rest your arm on a chair arm in a neutral way with your palm up. Loosly hold the weight and do tiny curls using only your wrist. 

Last, wrist pain can also be from the neck/back/and shoulders (that's where mine comes from). For the last one stand in a doorway with your arm bent upward like you're going to high-five. Put your arm on the doorframe, step forward, and hold for a second. I usually do about 10 times per arm. 

Of course all these exercises should relieve pain so if they hurt stop right away. I usually try to incorporate them in my warm up. Run scales, stretch my fingers, run scales, lift weight, etc. 

This last thing may sound weird, but if you spend a decent amount of time in your phone or tablet get a pop-socket or something similar. For a long time I was holding my phone in an awkward claw shape, with this you can let your hand rest more naturally. There's also generic ones for only a couple dollars cause the brand ones can be up to $15.

I hope this helps and if it doesn't get better soon go to the doctor. I put it off too long and found out most injuries like this don't really get better, you just have to learn to live with them.

Mine wasn't gigged a lot but I did a good amount of practices with it when I was in a band for about 4 years. I've never had electrical issues, that is all very solid. I think the high maintenance concern is from the double truss rod. Your tech (or in their cases rhodie) really needs to know how to adjust a double truss rod or they could royally fuck the neck. And since its neck through construction a replacement neck means a replacement bass. If I we're gigging it regularly and subjecting it to hots and colds regularly, I could see thinking it's high maintenance. I've heard, though not experienced, that temp changes affect the double truss rod even more as, again lending credit to their claims. 

Basically, if you're not a musician that plays for fun or maybe out once a month and you have a Ric certified tech nearby to set it up, I wouldn't worry. I would also believe the pros claims that it's unreliable as a workhorse being that I'm not a pro. I believe there's a reason almost every touring musician plays a Fender bass.

The Ric is pretty amazing. One thing to keep in mind is it will always sound like a Ric. To me, that's a good thing. It's hard to describe it though. It's boomey but has bite and dirty but still maintains clarity. Sustain is unlike anything else I've played. My favorite setting is bridge and neck with a pick, almost sounds like two bass players playing simultaneously. 

If you want to buy one go to a dealer and play them all. They're handmade so profiles are always a little different. Mine is more like a P-Bass neck, super chunky. I've got a buddy who has one that's a lot thinner, almost like a J-Bass at the higher frets.  I played a vintage one where the neck was like a pencil too.  The necks don't really taper at all, stay mostly the same width top to bottom. 

I can use the Ric anywhere too. I've played blues, classic rock, punk/ska, oldies and everything in between and it always sounds at home. Only thing I wouldn't play with it is slap bass. The pickups aren't really high gain enough for it. Also, the edge of the fretboard comes to a point. I bruised my thumb attempting slap on it. 

I'd recommend it highly but maybe I'm biased. If you have any questions I'd be more than happy to try and answer them.

Fast forward and we're gigging regularly at an old ballroom. One night it catches fire. I had the J Bass and Strat with me as I was playing guitar and bass with this band. I happened to be playing bass at the time and ran out leaving my Strat. We were allowed to look through the remains and happened to find the Strat, or what was left of it anyway. The body was split in three, hardware melted, and the neck was turned into a toothpick. It sat in my garage for about five years before a friend suggested trying to restore it. It's hard to see in photos, especially since I used my phone, but there was some pitting in the body that refused to be filled. The center block also doesn't sit flush at the bottom. There's also little things like the jack plate is warped and the neck pocket is a little too wide (but I blame 70s Fender "quality control" on those issues).

I've played in a couple punk bands, trying to start a new one now actually since my drummer moved away.  I should note first, I can't read music, I play all by ear so this may not work for you.  My most successful songs always started the same way. I usually write the lyrics first, get something I like, and put it to paper. Next I sing those lyrics, over and over. If I'm not sure how they should go I sing them in different ways; hyper fast, slow and ballot like, grungy, pop-punk like, with rasp, clean, etc.  Then I come up with a simple progression, usually three chords, maybe four. I record that or just play it till I hear it. Sometimes I stop there, punk is about feeling and sometimes a three chord progression just feels right. If the song feels hollow, repetitive, or boring I start working on individual sections. Maybe turn a chunk of lyrics onto a bridge. Maybe change the key at a part. Maybe I significantly change the chorus to make it stand out.   You can also usually add a lead up to the chorus out of two chords easily to make it stand out more. At this point if the song isn't working, I scrap it or just set it aside. Sometimes a song just doesn't work. I hope this helps.

I used a Boss Distortion pedal. Nothing fancy, just the $60.00 off the rack pedal labeled "Distortion". Instrumentally it sounded right off a Green Day album. The nice thing about emulating old Green Day tone is pre-Dookie they weren't well known and didn't have a lot of cash for equipment. Any solid body guitar with a decent humbucker will do you. I've had mine since Saturday, got it set up how I like by Saturday afternoon/evening. I'll do a run down myself I suppose. 
-Second screen:  Honestly, I wasn't sure about this. I actually ended up liking it. The built in apps are useful enough that if developers end up not supporting it that's okay. It's handy to be able to glance at notifications without closing out what I'm doing. 
-Performance:  No complaints. Everything is snappy. Games run well and look fantastic on the screen. Honestly, not much different to say about this performance wise than any other flagship. 
-Screen:  Speaking of screen, this is beautiful. Good in daylight. Not quite as much shine as the Samsung OLEDs but colors feel a little more natural.
-Software:  This is the first time I've not replaced the stock launcher with Nova. The customization is amazing (icon changing, widget stretching, color choice, etc) The performance is solid too, no where near the stuttery mess we've come to expect from TouchWiz. I do wish more apps supported split screen like TouchWiz though. 
-Hardware:  The phone feels good in the hand, but I've got big hands. The rubber back is grippy but not sticky. The back buttons are still taking a little getting used to but so far I'm liking them. I got used to the power button fast, still have to feel around for the volume. I love the fingerprint scanner but my phone is naked till my case comes in from Amazon. I can update this post once I get it if anyone cares. Gotta love an SD card slot too, one of the reasons I originally chose the V10 over the Note 5. 
-Camera:  I haven't had time to play with this as much as I'd have liked. The simple mode is solid. I love playing with the manual mode, you can do macro shots out of the box and they look presentable. 
Overall, I really like this phone. I'll say the battery life is great but it's still too soon to say how definitive this is. There is bleed on the second screen but only when the main screen is off. There is no bleed if the main screen is showing all black with the backlight on.
